text:
maria: Quick sync: noticed the continuous-batcher reacts poorly when seq-length distribution shifts mid-window. Batches either over-fill (latency spike) or under-fill (cost spike). We should standardize admission hints to let allocator make smarter packing decisions.

tariq: Agree. Current admission only gives token_estimate and timeout. We need richer signals but keep the surface tiny.

sophie: What about a compact AdmissionHint proto: window_hint_ms, seq_p50, seq_p95, prefetch_cost_bytes, priority_tier. Allocator can use seq_p95 to decide to tighten windows.

maria: Example: ```
AdmissionHint { window_hint_ms: 25, seq_p50: 64, seq_p95: 256, prefetch_cost_bytes: 12KB, priority_tier: 1 }
```

kevin: Love it. Two tradeoffs: extra fields increase churn on callers; and estimating seq_p95 on short-lived sessions is noisy.

tariq: For the noise problem we can make fields optional and allow admission to send streaming updates (per-epoch). Allocator should treat missing fields as unknown and use conservative defaults.

sophie: Also add a "batching_flex" enum: STRICT | FLEXIBLE. STRICT means do not enlarge window beyond hint; FLEXIBLE allows allocator to trade headroom for fill.

maria: That helps express critical vs opportunistic requests. We should tie STRICT to low-latency routes (e.g., interactive chat).

kevin: How does this interact with existing prefetch? Prefetch cost can block eviction decisions. If prefetch_cost_bytes is high, allocator might prioritize eviction differently.

tariq: Exactly. Allocator policy: rank candidates by (active_fill_value / prefetch_cost_bytes) to avoid evicting high-value warms. We can expose a simple scoring fn but keep it internal.

sophie: Ops ask: what metrics do we need to validate behavior? I want batch_fill_ratio, mean_window_ms, fill_by_tier, prefetch_eviction_rate, and moving p99 latency per tenant.

maria: Add drift_alert: when observed seq_p95 deviates > 2x from admission hint for N windows, trigger a tuned roll-up suggestion.

kevin: Implementation plan: 1) tiny proto change in admission path with optional fields, 2) allocator uses hint to choose window_ms and packing heuristics, 3) safe fallbacks for missing/unstable hints, 4) telemetry and alerting.

tariq: We should be careful about coupling: the admission service should NOT make hard guarantees. Hints are advisory; allocator keeps final say. Document the advisory semantics in the API contract.

sophie: Also add a quick A/B: enable hints for 10% of traffic for 2w to measure cost/latency delta. Include synthetic churn test to simulate seq distribution shift.

maria: Can someone take an owner for the allocator-side patch? I'd like the admission + SDK bits to be tiny and backwards-compatible.

kevin: I can take allocator side. Will prototype scoring and a graceful degrade path (use last-known good hint).

tariq: I'll add the hint fields and SDK changes. I'll also wire a lightweight drift detector in admission to smooth noisy stats.

runtime-bot: CI: 1748301400 - admission unit tests passed.

maria: Great. Let's keep defaults conservative (window_hint_ms=20, batching_flex=FLEXIBLE). We'll iterate after the A/B.

sophie: One more: document what "prefetch_cost_bytes" should include (KV entry + overhead). I'll draft a short doc for SDKs.

maria: Perfect. Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the A/B + chaos run. :rocket:
